title: Nvidia GeForce Now Launches in India With RTX 5080 Cloud Gaming Tiers
excerpt: Nvidia's cloud gaming service exits beta in India with three subscription tiers, RTX 5080-class hardware in Mumbai, and a free option — starting at ₹999 per month.
body:
• Nvidia's GeForce Now cloud gaming service is now fully available in India with monthly subscriptions starting at ₹999, following an open beta that began in April.
  • The Ultimate tier gives users access to RTX 5080-class hardware with up to 5K streaming at 360fps, powered by Blackwell-based SuperPOD servers in Mumbai.
  • A free ad-supported tier offers 1080p gaming with one-hour session limits, lowering the barrier for India's price-sensitive gaming market.
  • The service supports over 4,500 games from Steam, Epic Games Store, Xbox Game Pass, Ubisoft Connect, and GOG, with no need for expensive local hardware.

Nvidia has officially launched GeForce Now in India, bringing its cloud gaming platform out of beta and into full commercial availability. The service, which streams PC games from remote servers to nearly any internet-connected device, is now open to all users with monthly and daily subscription options — and critically, a free tier.

https://x.com/nvidia/status/2078228046465655279

The move marks a significant moment for India's gaming market, where dedicated gaming PCs remain a luxury for most players. With servers now live in Mumbai and pricing calibrated for the Indian market, Nvidia is betting that cloud gaming can bridge the gap between demand and affordability in one of the world's fastest-growing gaming communities.

Three Tiers, From Free to RTX 5080

GeForce Now in India offers three subscription levels. The free tier is ad-supported and provides 1080p streaming at 60fps with sessions capped at one hour — practical for quick rounds or testing your internet connection. The Performance tier costs ₹999 per month (or ₹399 for a day pass) and bumps resolution to 1440p at 60fps with six-hour sessions. At the top, the Ultimate tier costs ₹1,999 per month (₹799 per day) and delivers RTX 5080-class hardware capable of streaming at up to 5K resolution at 360fps, with support for DLSS 4, Nvidia Reflex, and Cloud G-Sync.

Both paid tiers include 100GB of cloud storage and are subject to a 100-hour monthly playtime cap. An additional 200GB of persistent storage is available for ₹299. Payments can be made via UPI, removing a friction point that has historically limited digital subscriptions in India.

"India is home to one of the world's most dynamic and rapidly expanding gaming communities. With the launch of GeForce NOW in India, we are enabling gamers to experience RTX 5080-class performance instantly without the cost or complexity of high-end hardware."

— Vishal Dhupar, Managing Director, Nvidia Asia-South

Blackwell-Powered Infrastructure in Mumbai

The India deployment runs on Nvidia's Blackwell-based RTX 5080 SuperPOD infrastructure housed in Mumbai data centres. Each cloud instance delivers up to 62 teraflops of compute performance with a 48GB frame buffer, enabling advanced ray tracing, AI-driven rendering, and DLSS features. Nvidia claims the setup is 2.8 times faster than previous-generation hardware and more than three times the performance of leading gaming consoles.

The Ultimate tier's Cinematic Quality Streaming mode uses AV1 encoding with AI-based video enhancements, 4:4:4 chroma subsampling, and 10-bit HDR for improved clarity and colour accuracy. A lower-latency mode pushes 1080p at 360fps with latency claimed to be under 30 milliseconds — a figure that will depend heavily on the player's ISP and proximity to the Mumbai servers.

A Library Without the Download

GeForce Now does not sell games. Instead, it connects to players' existing libraries on Steam, Epic Games Store, Xbox Game Pass, Ubisoft Connect, GOG, and Battle.net. The catalogue currently includes over 4,500 supported titles, with more than 100 free-to-play games such as Counter-Strike 2, alongside major titles like Cyberpunk 2077 and Forza Horizon 5. Nvidia says new games will be added weekly.

An Install-to-Play feature powered by Nvidia's NVMesh technology allows supported titles to be downloaded to cloud storage for faster access, reducing load times for returning players. This addresses one of the common complaints about cloud gaming — waiting for games to initialise on each session.

Why India, Why Now

Nvidia's timing is deliberate. Steam's user base in India has grown roughly 150 percent over the past four to five years, and average download speeds have reached around 50 Mbps according to Steam's own telemetry. The infrastructure is finally in place for cloud gaming to work reliably.

For Indian gamers and the broader diaspora community, the appeal is straightforward: access to high-end PC gaming without the upfront cost of hardware that can run into lakhs of rupees. With GPU prices remaining elevated globally, a ₹1,999 monthly subscription for RTX 5080-class performance represents a fundamentally different value proposition than buying and maintaining a gaming rig.

Beta participants will receive a 20 percent discount on their first three months of a recurring membership. The waitlist has been fully removed, and all tiers are now available for immediate sign-up on the GeForce Now India website.
